title: An executive's first day
audience: Someone who decides and delegates. Short answers, decisions first.

steps.goal: Get the picture of one project
steps.see: A short summary with the status, the risks and the decisions waiting for you.
steps.why: You get the state of play in under a minute.

steps.see: Up to three lines: the one thing that needs you now, why, and what to try after.
steps.why: Your time goes to the decision that is actually waiting.

steps.see: One waiting item at a time with the choices: close it, keep it, drop it or push it to a date.
steps.why: A backlog gets cleared in minutes instead of growing.

steps.see: Each loose note from your inbox, with the project it probably belongs to, for you to accept or change.
steps.why: Thoughts caught in passing end up where someone will act on them.

steps.say: /gt:gt-query what is the biggest open risk
steps.see: A short answer with the note it came from.
steps.why: You ask in your own words; nobody has to prepare a report.

steps.see: A brief first: what moved, what was decided, what is blocked, then the saved notes.
steps.why: The record of today exists without you writing it.
